description: Cacik is a classic Turkish appetizer, a refreshing yogurt and cucumber dip perfect for hot summer days or as part of a mezze spread. Made with strained yogurt, grated cucumber, garlic, fresh mint, and a drizzle of olive oil, it offers a delightful balance of creamy, tangy, and herbal flavors. This cooling dip is an essential accompaniment to grilled meats, pilafs, or simply enjoyed with warm pita bread.

ingredients.notes: full-fat for best texture, or Greek yogurt

instructions.title: Prepare the Cucumber
instructions.text: Grate the English cucumber. Place the grated cucumber in a clean kitchen towel or cheesecloth and squeeze out as much excess water as possible. This crucial step prevents the cacik from becoming watery.

instructions.title: Mince Garlic and Chop Mint
instructions.text: Finely mince the garlic cloves. Thoroughly wash and finely chop the fresh mint leaves. Set aside for later use.

instructions.title: Combine Yogurt and Garlic
instructions.text: In a medium mixing bowl, add the strained yogurt. Add the minced garlic to the yogurt and whisk gently until the garlic is evenly distributed and the yogurt is smooth.

instructions.title: Add Cucumber and Mint
instructions.text: Fold in the squeezed grated cucumber and the chopped fresh mint into the yogurt mixture. Mix well to combine all ingredients.

instructions.title: Season and Adjust Consistency
instructions.text: Add salt to taste, starting with 1/2 teaspoon and adjusting as needed. Gradually stir in the cold water, 1/4 to 1/2 cup, until you achieve your desired consistency. Cacik should be pourable but still creamy, not too thick or too thin.

instructions.title: Chill and Garnish
instructions.text: Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. This allows the flavors to meld beautifully and ensures the dip is perfectly chilled. Before serving, drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil and sprinkle with dried mint, if using, for an authentic touch.

tips: For an authentic creamy texture, use traditional Turkish strained yogurt (süzme yoğurt) or good quality Greek yogurt. If using regular yogurt, strain it through a cheesecloth for several hours to remove excess whey.
Don't skip squeezing the excess water from the grated cucumber; this is crucial to prevent your cacik from becoming watery and to maintain its rich, thick consistency.
Cacik tastes best when chilled for at least 30 minutes before serving, allowing the flavors to fully meld. It can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 days.
